rules.title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers coordinated pricing algorithms that use non-public competitor data (less than 90 days old) to set or recommend rents or occupancy rates for residential dwelling units in Berkeley; does not regulate rent amounts or general property management software using public data; research, testing, and training for software development using competitor data excluded from operational recommendation
rules.exemptions: (a) Aggregated and anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend specific prices; (b) Products for establishing rent or income limits per affordable housing guidelines; (c) Software for market research, appraisals, or research/testing/training that does not use competitor data as operational input for recommendations
rules.sanctions: Civil action by City Attorney for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation (each separate month and each separate unit constitutes separate violation); aggrieved tenants may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing party attorney fees awarded
